source.title: Towards a Foundation-Model Paradigm for Aerodynamic Prediction in Three-dimensional Design
source.authors: Yunjia Yang; Babak Gholami; C. Gurbuz; Mohammad Rashed; N. Thürey

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether downstream aerodynamic prediction improves with the size of the pretrained model or dataset, using prediction error rather than language-model cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other scaling-related results, including held-out aerodynamic prediction errors across model and pretraining-data sizes (Fig. 9), but those are not downstream-task results. It does not fit or test power laws, extrapolate small-run fits, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Rows below cover the downstream scaling comparisons in Fig. 13.
record.test_reason: This is an aerodynamic surrogate study, not a language-model study. It varies model size (1.0M–14.5M) and pretraining data (2.6k–23.4k flow fields) and reports that error falls with diminishing returns. It fits no power law, extrapolates no fitted law and tests no compute-optimal split. The system and measure (surface-flow error of a CFD surrogate) are not what V6 names (downstream tasks of language models). With only 3–4 points per axis and no functional-form fit, nothing bears on V5's power-law form. Kaplan et al. is cited [50] only as motivation for scaling the base model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: larger pretrained models and larger pretraining datasets both improve downstream CRM prediction, with dataset size having the more pronounced effect in the tested range, at higher computational cost.
record.recipe_differences: No language-model scaling-law recipe or comparable cross-entropy fitting procedure is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative effect of model size versus pretraining dataset size differs: the authors report a more pronounced impact from dataset size in the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream CRM surface-flow error falls as the pretrained base model gets larger or sees more pretraining data. In the tested range, data size has the larger effect (Fig. 13, SFE about 0.606% down to 0.362%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In scientific-ML surrogates, downstream fine-tuned error decreases monotonically with base-model size and pretraining-data size.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out pretraining SFE falls with more data for S/M/L models (about 0.217% down to 0.110%), with diminishing gains. The authors attribute these to S-model capacity and to a fixed step budget (Fig. 9). No rows record this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-text surrogate pretraining error improves with model and data size, but saturates under a fixed number of steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream fine-tuning error shows near-linear improvement with fine-tuning data size on a log axis (Fig. 14, 0.860% down to 0.231%). The authors extrapolate that from-scratch training would need O(10^4) samples to match fine-tuning. No rows record this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning data scaling in an aerodynamic surrogate is roughly log-linear and can be extrapolated.

record.problems: The downstream scaling comparison is limited to the tested aerodynamic task and ranges. Fig. 13 supplies the plotted values, while the prose reports qualitative trends; no scaling-law fit, extrapolation, or uncertainty for these comparisons is stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant downstream scaling rows left out. Held-out pretraining error scaling results in Fig. 9 are not downstream-task results and are not catalogued here.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss or power-law fit.
No small-run fit used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and data.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count; only width (hidden dim 16/32/64) is varied, and that changes size.
Other-domain (CFD surrogate) scaling is reported, but there is no power-law form, fit or exponent, and only 3–4 points per axis.
No language-model downstream tasks; no prediction from pretraining loss.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and its V6 'supports' labels are withdrawn: V6 concerns language-model downstream predictability, and this study fits no scaling law. Fig. 13 point-to-axis assignment cannot be read reliably from the extracted text. The parameter count for the L model is inconsistent (10.5M in the text, 14.5M in the figures).

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy or power-law fit in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and training tokens is tested.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns aerodynamic prediction, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
Tests downstream aerodynamic prediction across pretrained model sizes and pretraining dataset sizes, but not language-model downstream tasks, predictability from pretraining loss, or extrapolation.
Does not compare scaling-law exponents or show dependence of such fits on setup or fitting choices.
